content.user_title: Build Better Next.js App Router Projects
content.value_statement: Next.js App Router projects often suffer from unclear component boundaries and inconsistent data fetching. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise patterns for routing, caching, metadata, and server actions.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Server Components or Client Components.
Summarizes App Router data fetching and cache strategy choices.
Lists common route file conventions and route organization patterns.
Provides API route handler and server action guidance.
Covers performance, metadata, loading states, and error boundaries.
Shows a simple App Router project structure reference.
limitations: It is a guidance skill and does not inspect a repository automatically.
It does not run tests, install packages, or execute commands.
It may not cover every feature added after the skill was written.
It gives patterns, not full application architecture decisions.

use_cases.title: Plan a New App Router Feature
use_cases.description: Map component boundaries, data fetching, loading states, and route files before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review a Next.js Refactor
use_cases.description: Check whether a migration uses Server Components, caching, metadata, and route handlers in consistent ways.

use_cases.title: Teach App Router Basics
use_cases.description: Create a concise checklist for developers who are learning modern Next.js project structure.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Component Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature idea. Decide which parts should be Server Components and which need Client Components. Explain each boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page requirement. Recommend the fetch strategy, cache behavior, loading state, and error boundary for the App Router route.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Route Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this proposed App Router folder structure. Identify missing route files, route groups, metadata needs, and navigation risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize App Router Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing Next.js App Router workflow. Prioritize changes for caching, server actions, bundle size, metadata, and API route design.

output_examples.input: A dashboard page needs account data, filters, and a settings form.
output: Use a Server Component parent for account data.
Move filters and form interactions into small Client Components.
Use loading and error boundaries for the route.

output_examples.input: A product page needs fresh prices but stable marketing copy.
output: Use dynamic or revalidated fetching for price data.
Keep metadata generation close to the route.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce client bundle size.
output: Start with Server Components by default.
Move only interactive controls to the client.
Use dynamic imports for heavy optional UI.

best_practices: Start with Server Components, then add Client Components only for interactivity.
Choose caching behavior deliberately for each data source and route.
Use route files for loading, errors, not found states, and shared layouts.
anti_patterns: Marking broad component trees with use client without a clear reason.
Fetching all data in client components when server fetching is possible.
Skipping metadata, loading states, and error boundaries until late in development.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete Next.js applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides best practice guidance that an AI assistant can apply during planning, review, or implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with Server Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when Server Components should be the default and when Client Components are required.

faq.question: Does it cover App Router file conventions?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common files such as page, layout, loading, error, and not found routes.

faq.question: Can it improve performance reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights image optimization, dynamic imports, code splitting, and cache choices.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or modify projects by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-only and requests read, write, edit, glob, and grep tools.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives concise instructions that these assistants can use when working on Next.js App Router code.
